newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe says rates could go lower.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe says rates could go lower.

text.p: Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Friday that, with inflation so low, interests rates could go a little lower.
"With the weak inflation that we have today, it would be useful to go even farther in lowering rates," Juppe said in an interview with the French daily Le Figaro.
"I don't believe what I say to be sacrilege. I imagine that the governor of the Bank of France shares my opinion," he said in the interview to be published in Saturday's editions.
The text of the interview was given Reuters on Friday.
In the Interview, Juppe also said France's relations were "excellent" with Germany and its Bundesbank central bank.
